channel.title: Attention Span
channel.description: Today's AI news, traced back to its roots.

item.title: Reuters: Jensen Huang also had a relationship with a second Nvidia employee before resigning, sources say
item.description: Reuters, citing two people familiar, reports ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee before he resigned. Reuters reports, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee. Reuters is withholding her name. Nvidia announced Thursday that Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately. This followed reports of an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials reportedly concluded was a Chinese spy, and a second affair with a direct report. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent one. Harvey Jones becomes first board chair. Nvidia shares fell more than 13% in early trading. Democrats have launched an investigation.

item.title: Report claims six Chinese AI models show fingerprints of export-controlled Blackwell GPUs
item.description: A forensic analysis by Will DePue claims six models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group carry numerical patterns matching NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. Will DePue of Unemployment Labs analysed published model weights. He reports that six models released since April 2026 from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group match Blackwell hardware, while earlier models match the older Hopper generation. For DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi K3, the match was also confirmed on physical Blackwell chips. The author says this supports, without proving, that Blackwell did the training. It does not show where the chips were, how access was obtained, or whether export controls were broken. The author estimates each run needed roughly 1,500 to 3,500 Blackwell GPUs.

item.title: Lawmaker says Nvidia privately said chip tracking is possible, despite industry group's doubts
item.description: Rep. Bill Foster says Nvidia representatives told him privately that Chip Security Act tracking is technically possible, though nothing was put in writing. Illinois Rep. Bill Foster, a cosponsor of the Chip Security Act, told MIT Technology Review that Nvidia representatives said it could implement the bill's anti-smuggling measures. He says they never put anything in writing. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, which includes Nvidia, called the mandates "new, untested, and potentially infeasible." Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment on Foster's account. The act would require chip location checks through inspections, company attestations, or ping-based mechanisms. It is one of three chip-security bills being considered for the Senate's National Defense Authorization Act. Separately, Bloomberg sources say OpenAI told lawmakers it would support a bipartisan effort to curb China's access to AI chips.

item.title: Claude Code v2.1.323 adds experimental Code Mode and plugin version limits
item.description: Claude Code v2.1.323 adds Code Mode, where Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools, plus plugin version checks and many sign-in and stability fixes. Anthropic released Claude Code v2.1.323. It adds Code Mode, an experimental opt-in in which Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools. Organizations can turn it off. Plugins can now set engines["claude-code"] in plugin.json, and plugins outside the stated version range are not installed, updated or loaded. The claude plugin validate command now type checks a plugin's TypeScript hooks module. Hooks that run long in claude -p and SDK sessions send a progress heartbeat every 30 seconds. The release also fixes many sign-in problems for background sessions, a memory spike after a very large file change, and /compact summarizing away an unanswered message.

item.title: Apple's Foundation Models framework adds server models, Dynamic Profiles, image input and an fm CLI
item.description: Apple's Foundation Models framework now reaches server models like Claude and Gemini through one Swift API, and adds Dynamic Profiles, image understanding, Evaluations and an fm command line tool. Apple describes the Foundation Models framework as a native Swift API for using large language models in apps. It gives direct access to Apple Foundation Models on-device and in Private Cloud Compute. It now extends to server models like Claude and Gemini through the same API. Model providers can ship a Swift package that conforms to the Language Model protocol. New pieces include Dynamic Profiles, image understanding, an Evaluations framework, and the fm command line tool in macOS 27. Open source options include a utilities package and a Python SDK.

item.title: Synth developers report weeks-long Apple App Store delays and rejections they blame on AI
item.description: Synth developers say Apple's app review is stalling for weeks and issuing odd rejections, as an estimated 10–20 new iOS music apps arrive daily. Synth Anatomy reports that a flood of AI-made iOS music apps, estimated at 10–20 new apps a day, is straining Apple's app review. Apple's guidelines say it reviews at least 50% of submissions in under 24 hours and 90% in under 48 hours. Developers including AudioThing, Igor Vasiliev and Sugar Bytes say apps sat in review for weeks. Unfiltered Audio's Michael Hetrick says Sinusoidal Run Rhythm was rejected 4 times and he believes Apple uses AI for reviews. Marek Dendes says CRUX Synth was rejected four times in a row, with no reply to his appeals.

item.title: Families protest in seven cities over Google's AI in schools, no AI-free Search option
item.description: Families protested in seven US cities against Google's AI in schools after Google confirmed students cannot use Google Search without AI. Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday. They object to what they see as Google's bid to entrench its AI models in schools. The backlash follows a Google statement last week confirming there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. Google said it was giving schools "more choice, not less" by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default. It would not offer Search without AI. Parents worried that students would have to remember to add "-ai" to every query. In Chicago, dozens of protesters marched to Google's downtown office despite cold, rainy weather.

item.title: Nebius plans $40 billion in 2027 spending as Microsoft site delays mount
item.description: Nebius laid out $40 billion in planned 2027 spending, funded by prepayments and contract-backed loans, while a delayed Microsoft site in New Jersey raises risk. On its third-quarter call, Nebius said it plans $40 billion in spending for 2027, far above Wall Street expectations. It expects prepayments plus asset-backed financing to cover up to 85% of the $40 to $45 billion capex. Its Microsoft contract is worth up to $19.4 billion, but the Vineland, New Jersey site is months behind. Only just over half of that capacity is planned by year end, with the rest in Q2 2027. Nebius cut its 2026 revenue forecast by $200 million to $3 billion. Shares ended the day down 17%.

item.title: SGLang-Neuron brings SGLang serving to AWS Trainium via Deep Learning Container
item.description: Amazon says SGLang-Neuron is publicly available, letting developers serve models and run RL rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium through a Deep Learning Container. Amazon announced that SGLang-Neuron is publicly available through an AWS Deep Learning Container. RadixArk released it with Annapurna Labs. You can serve models and generate reinforcement learning (RL) rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium using the same SGLang interface. It is an out-of-tree plugin that runs on native PyTorch. SGLang core keeps the API server, request lifecycle, RadixAttention and prefix-cache bookkeeping. The plugin handles Trainium-specific models, attention, mixture of experts (MoE) and the graph runner. It also supports PD disaggregation, using NIXL over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA). The walkthrough serves openai/gpt-oss-120b on a Trainium3 EC2 instance.

item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim
item.description: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO, president and board member after a board investigation into reported affairs, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president and board member of Nvidia, effective immediately, according to a statement dated November 12, 2026. The Verge reports the board had opened an investigation into multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a direct report and one with an alleged Chinese spy. The New York Times reported a second affair on Wednesday, and a board meeting that night ended with his resignation. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Harvey Jones is the first Chair of the Board. The Decoder reports the scandal wiped out $1.4 trillion in market value.

item.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast model for coding and agent workflows
item.description: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, built for fast execution in coding and agent tasks, priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. Google DeepMind launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen on Nov 12, 2026. It is built for rapid execution in everyday coding and agentic workflows. It scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level, against 50 for Gemini 4 Argon, and 54 at xhigh. Pricing is flat across a 1 million-token context window: $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. Google also added Orchestrator in Google Antigravity, which switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen in one session. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 it used 24% less quota and finished 19% faster. Against Gemini 3.8 Flash, Hydrogen finishes tasks 2.5 times faster.

item.title: Anthropic Announces Initial Public Offering Timeline and Financial Highlights
item.description: Anthropic announced its initial public offering timeline, offering Class A common stock on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. Anthropic announced details for its initial public offering of Class A common stock on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. The roadshow starts on November 10th. Subject to regulatory clearance, the final share price is expected to be set on November 18th, and trading is expected to begin on November 19th. As of September 30, 2026, the company reported $17.0 billion in revenue, over 11,900 customers with at least $100K trailing twelve month revenue, and a net loss of $23.3 billion driven largely by a non-cash charge related to convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs.

item.title: United Airlines Bans AI Agents From Booking Flights
item.description: United Airlines banned personal artificial intelligence agents from booking flights, citing security risks, privacy concerns, and potential federal rule violations. United Airlines announced a ban on artificial intelligence agents making flight reservations on behalf of travelers. The carrier cited security risks, privacy concerns, and the possibility that third-party AI tools could violate federal rules. Sharing credentials with personal AI assistants can expose sensitive information. It can also lead to unintended purchases or account changes. Using AI tools to check in could also violate federal regulations requiring travelers to verify that luggage lacks banned substances. United is restricting access on its digital platforms and via travel agencies. Southwest Airlines has taken a different approach by making its inventory viewable to ChatGPT users.

item.title: OpenAI research: training choices make frontier models' reasoning harder to monitor
item.description: OpenAI's safety team says four training steps, including architecture and reinforcement learning, make GPT-6 Astra's chains of thought harder to monitor, and that this is tied to capability and cost. OpenAI's safety team studied models from GPT-5 through GPT-6 Astra to find why chains of thought are harder for monitors to read. It traced the problem to four main causes across the training cycle. Silent reasoning without a scratchpad rises with base model capability. One of three anonymized architectures, "Architecture 2", favored silent multi-step reasoning. Reinforcement learning now increases control over the reasoning log in Astra-class and internal "Terra" models. Student models inherit a teacher's high CoT controllability. OpenAI says the loss of transparency is not purely a law of nature. A smaller model that reasons at greater length can be easier to monitor, but it raises compute costs.

item.title: Azure Content Understanding Adds GPT-5.6, GPT-6, and GPT-6.1 Models
item.description: Azure Content Understanding now supports new model families, giving developers more choices for document, text, speech, and video workflows. Azure Content Understanding now supports the GPT-5.6, GPT-6, and GPT-6.1 model families. This update expands options for document, text, speech, and video workflows alongside the existing GPT-5 series. Microsoft updated its model recommendations and shared evaluation data. For standard document extraction, users can start with GPT-6.1 Sol, add GPT-6 Luna for low token costs, or test GPT-6 Astra when quality improvements justify a premium. The service allows testing with a schema only or with labeled examples to balance quality and cost before changing model budgets.

item.title: Huawei releases MACaQ internal quantizer for local inference
item.description: Huawei released MACaQ, a model-agnostic quantizer for local inference supporting text, image, video, and audio models across multiple backends. Huawei released MACaQ, an internal quantizer for local inference across text, image, video, and audio models. It supports backends like llama.cpp, vLLM, Diffusers, and PyTorch. The tool can quantize a 122B-parameter model in 64 minutes using 32.5 GB of device memory. It matches Llama-3-8B perplexity with 11 times less quantization time compared to other methods. The project includes MACaQ-R for refining weight codes in quantized GGUF formats and provides W4A4 support for various generation tasks. MACaQ is licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

item.title: Amazon Announces Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description: AWS announced the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, allowing custom code to search the web with a single API call. Amazon introduced the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This new API lets developer code search the web using a single call through AWS SDKs or the AWS Command Line Interface. It returns ranked results from an Amazon-operated web index with text extracts, page titles, URLs, and publication times when available. Requests are signed with AWS Signature Version 4 credentials. It serves non-agent use cases, custom orchestration frameworks, and applications requiring real-time web results without setting up a full AgentCore Gateway stack.

item.title: AWS updates AgentCore runtime with faster starts and larger agent sessions
item.description: AWS announced updates to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime: sessions start up to 15x faster, scale to 4x more compute, and run up to 68% more efficiently. AWS announced updates to AgentCore runtime, the managed compute layer of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Every session still runs in its own hardware-isolated Firecracker MicroVM, with its own identity, policy, and audit trail. Sessions now start up to 15x faster, scale to 4x more compute, and run up to 68% more efficiently. Sessions go up to 8 vCPUs and 32 GB, with container images up to 10 GB. They start in under 2 seconds, independent of image size and concurrency, so warm pools and pre-provisioned clusters are no longer needed. Customers Coinbase, Mission Cloud, Zuora and Rescale gave feedback.

item.title: ElevenLabs releases Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live speech-to-text models
item.description: ElevenLabs released Scribe v3 for recorded audio and Scribe v3 Live for real-time use, built for crosstalk and background noise. ElevenLabs has released two speech-to-text models, Scribe v3 for pre-recorded audio and Scribe v3 Live for low-latency real-time use. The company says Scribe v3 cuts word errors by about 25 percent versus its predecessor across 102 languages. Artificial Analysis benchmarks put Scribe v3 among the most accurate models, but Microsoft and xAI models run many times faster and cost roughly half as much. Scribe v3 Live analyzes conversational context to tell when a speaker has finished. Both models are available through the ElevenAPI and the ElevenAgents platform.

item.title: Using OpenAI Codex on Amazon Bedrock with Existing AWS Practices
item.description: Developers can use OpenAI Codex on Amazon Bedrock while fitting model paths into existing AWS identity, IAM, and observability practices. Developers increasingly use OpenAI Codex with Amazon Bedrock to explore unfamiliar code, make changes, and handle repetitive engineering work. Platform teams can make these tools available without creating a second model-access, identity, and operations stack. Codex runs on the developer workstation while model requests reach Amazon Bedrock. Organizations can start with a small, least-privilege pilot using Native AWS Access, AgentCore Gateway, or an LLM Gateway. Before expanding access, teams must review supported models by region, configure workforce identity providers like Okta with IAM Identity Center, validate runtime access, and run a safe test task.

item.title: smolmaxxing runs 8B and 16B models on about 1 GB of RAM
item.description: An open-source llama.cpp patch called smolmaxxing runs 8B and 16B mixture-of-experts models on about 1 GB of RAM by streaming weights from flash. smolmaxxing is a patch on llama.cpp that aims to run the biggest language model possible on small, old hardware such as TV boxes, old tablets, single-board computers and routers. Two devices are covered so far, and both run 8B and 16B mixture-of-experts models on about 1 GB of RAM. It keeps part of each model in memory and reads the rest from flash as needed. Other techniques include a 1-bit lookup-table kernel, dropping rarely used vocabulary output rows, and streaming for dense models bigger than RAM. All numbers were measured on the devices. Stock llama.cpp cannot load the model files.

item.title: Report Looks at Potential Nvidia CEO Candidates
item.description: A Bloomberg report looks at potential candidates to replace Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. Nvidia Corporation is searching for a replacement for Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. Bloomberg published a look at potential candidates for the role at the world's most valuable chipmaker. The candidates mentioned include CFO Colette Kress, CUDA inventor Ian Buck, Arm CEO Rene Haas, and Apple Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji.

item.title: Report: Jev used for rapid document ranking and UI prediction
item.description: At the AI Engineer Code Summit, Jev powered fast document chunk ranking and a time-off UI filler. The AI Engineer Code Summit highlighted system one models, non‑generative models that return structured choices, scores, or probabilities and are faster and cheaper than reasoning LLMs. Diogo Almeida, co‑founder and CEO of TypeSafe AI, introduced Jev, released in September, as "reliable intelligence" for automating tasks. Glean uses Jev for zero‑shot flexibility without fine‑tuning. UiPath demonstrated a Jev tournament that ranked document chunks in under a second, even with thousands of calls. Workday showed a prototype where Jev pre‑fills a time‑off card while the user types.

item.title: Google Launches Tabletop AI Personal Planning Platform
item.description: Google launched Tabletop, an experimental AI platform for personal planning and coordination hubs, in beta via a waitlist. Google launched Tabletop, an experimental AI platform. The platform builds customizable and collaborative personal planning and coordination hubs. Tabletop provides customizable, collaborative spaces for personal planning needs. The release is currently in beta and is available via a waitlist. Jess Weatherbed reported the news for The Verge on November 12, 2026.

item.title: Anthropic adds Sheets, Whiteboards and Interactive Connectors to Claude, with Meetings coming soon
item.description: Anthropic is adding spreadsheet, whiteboard, dashboard and partner app features to Claude, and says a call-joining Meetings tool is coming soon. Anthropic is adding several collaboration features to the Claude app. Claude Sheets lets teams create and edit spreadsheets with AI assistance, including formulas and multiple tabs. Claude Whiteboards lets teams brainstorm and have Claude summarize the ideas. Claude Data, formerly Dashboards, connects to tools like Snowflake and Salesforce to build dashboards and data visualizations. Interactive Connectors let partners like Adobe, Atlassian, and Salesforce embed their apps in Claude. Anthropic says Claude Meetings, which can join calls and take notes, is launching soon. Enterprise customers get audit logs, isolated virtual machines, and a compliance API.

item.title: Anthropic S-1: each of seven co-founders to sell 3,378,378 shares in IPO
item.description: Anthropic's S-1 says each of its seven co-founders will sell 3,378,378 shares, about $250 million each at the $74 midpoint. Anthropic's new S-1 filing shows each of its seven co-founders plans to sell 3,378,378 shares in the IPO. The initial price range is $70 to $78 a share. At $74, each founder would take in just shy of $250 million. At $70 it is just over $236 million, and at $78 just under $264 million. After the sale, each will own about 3.2% of Class A shares, roughly 22% together. Each also gets one Class F share with supervoting rights. Together the founders will control 51.1% of the votes. Financial Times sources say bankers are weighing a higher IPO price after heavy demand.

item.title: NYT reports Amazon and Google own 25%+ of Anthropic as it prepares to IPO
item.description: The New York Times reports that Amazon and Google collectively own 25%+ of Anthropic, which is preparing to IPO, and their stakes could gain hundreds of billions in value. Karen Weise of the New York Times reports that Anthropic is preparing to IPO. Amazon and Google are the largest investors in the A.I. start-up. Together they own 25%+ of the company. Amazon's $18B investment could reach $250B+ in value. Google's $33B investment could hit $140B. The report says their shares could gain hundreds of billions of dollars in value. The source is a Techmeme summary of the Times piece, dated November 11, 2026. It does not say when an IPO would happen or confirm that one will take place.

item.title: Google Announces Gemini Decisions API and Gemini Decision 1 Model
item.description: Google launched the Gemini Decisions API, powered by the Gemini Decision 1 model, to evaluate up to 1,000 questions in a single pass. Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API powered by the Gemini Decision 1 model. The tool evaluates up to 1,000 yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring questions in a single pass across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs. It computes confidence scores with an end-to-end latency of 150 to 250 ms at $0.10 per 1M input tokens with zero output tokens billed. The model supports contexts up to 256K tokens. Teams across Google use the API for dynamic model routing, rapid design iteration, emoji selection, and safety checks.

item.title: Google DeepMind Announces AlphaGenome 2 for Cell-Level DNA Analysis
item.description: Google DeepMind has unveiled AlphaGenome 2, a conditional DNA sequence model designed to predict how genetic variants affect specific human cell types. Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2, a next-generation DNA sequence model that bridges single-cell biology and human genetics. Unlike its predecessor that used parallel bulk tissue predictions, AlphaGenome 2 is a conditional model taking a target biological condition as input alongside a million-letter DNA sequence. Trained on over 107 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues, the model identifies nearly twice as many variants that change gene expression in cells. It is available for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API and in private preview for commercial research.

item.title: OpenAI Q3 revenue reportedly hits $10 billion, still behind Anthropic's $17 billion
item.description: Reports say OpenAI's Q3 revenue grew about 50 percent to $10 billion, but it posted a $10.9 billion adjusted operating loss and trails Anthropic. The Wall Street Journal and The Information report that OpenAI grew revenue about 50 percent quarter over quarter in Q3 to $10 billion. Adjusted operating losses rose from $10.1 billion to $10.9 billion. Anthropic brought in $17 billion over the same period, with an operating loss of $567 million. OpenAI is cutting prices on new models, has put more resources into Codex, and hired Dali Rajic as head of sales. Greg Brockman said the enterprise business doubled in Q3. ChatGPT has 100 million paying subscribers.

item.title: OpenAI launches Business Hub in ChatGPT for company profiles and agents
item.description: OpenAI launched a beta Business Hub in ChatGPT where companies can verify profiles, track user interactions and, if eligible, launch a business agent. OpenAI rolled out a Business Hub in ChatGPT on Tuesday. Companies can create business profiles to verify and update information about their products and services. The feature is in beta. Eligible companies can also launch a business agent that lets ChatGPT users ask questions about the business and its products. The Hub gives limited insights, including profile views, business mentions and website clicks. Profiles must be verified, but OpenAI did not share specifics. The Decoder reports that Business Agents are for eligible US e-commerce providers. In March, OpenAI retired an earlier commission-based checkout effort.

item.title: Claroc research says Grok Build share links leak confidential data, including SpaceXSI's own
item.description: Security firm Claroc says Grok Build share links let anyone enumerate thousands of live projects and see sensitive data, including from 24 SpaceXSI apps. Research from security firm Claroc shows that Grok Build, a vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI, is leaking data from thousands of its users. The leak comes through links that let users share their apps. Grok randomizes the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can reach the data. A design decision by the platform's developers defeats this and lets anyone enumerate thousands of live projects. Except in rare cases, clicking a link opens the app and shows all its data. Exposed data includes internal business plans, ad proposals, medical exam results and employee names and ID numbers. Claroc found 24 apps built by SpaceXSI itself, including a confidential onboarding plan and a sales territory map of 594 accounts.

item.title: Microsoft researchers describe Lazarus, a no-training backdoor that edits fewer than 10 neurons
item.description: Microsoft researchers say reprogramming fewer than 10 dormant neurons can backdoor an LLM agent without training, triggered by cues like a date change. Microsoft researchers describe "Lazarus," a backdoor technique that reprograms dormant neurons in an AI model. They find that weight-reprogramming fewer than 10 dormant neurons in an LLM is enough to backdoor an agent, with no training. The model passes standard evals and acts normally until a trigger appears, such as the clock passing midnight into 2027. The agent can then download and run attacker code with its access. The researchers say frontier agents can spot anomalous weight edits if asked, but no scan can prove a model is safe. Reliable detection needs diffing against the original weights, so provenance matters.

item.title: Point72's Cubist alleges fired analyst used Claude and Codex to steal code
item.description: Point72's quant unit Cubist alleges in a lawsuit that a fired lead research analyst used Claude and Codex to steal source code before joining a competitor. Bloomberg reports on a lawsuit filing by Cubist, the quantitative trading unit of Point72 Asset Management. Cubist claims a former lead research analyst, who was fired, used Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's Codex to steal source code. The suit says this happened before the analyst left for a competitor. These are allegations from the filing. The source text does not say how the tools were used, what code was taken, or how the analyst or the competitor responded.

item.title: Anthropic Claims AI Porting Reduces Chip Switch Time
item.description: Anthropic claims its AI model ported Claude to AMD GPUs in three days, reducing reliance on Nvidia's CUDA. Anthropic stated in an investor presentation that it now runs Claude on four major chip families using a multi-chip strategy. According to the company, its frontier model Mythos ported nearly 100 percent of the kernels to AMD GPUs in three days, instead of the usual six to twelve months, with almost no human intervention. These figures have not been independently verified. If accurate, the claims suggest that software overhead could shrink, allowing companies to switch more easily between chip providers and focus on price-performance ratios. Both Nvidia and AMD have financial ties to Anthropic.

item.title: Atuin 18.24 Introduces Threads to Sync Coding Agent Sessions
item.description: Atuin 18.24 introduces Threads, allowing users to search, resume, and fork coding agent sessions across multiple machines. Atuin has released version 18.24 with a new feature called Threads. Threads enables developers to search agent sessions across machines, resume them anywhere, or fork sessions into different agent harnesses. Supported agents include Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Omp, and OpenCode. The sync engine uses end-to-end encryption, and users can use a hosted sync server, run their own, or keep sessions local. Additionally, Model Context Protocol integration allows agents to search and reference previous sessions automatically.

item.title: New York opens registration portal as RAISE Act AI safety law nears
item.description: New York opened a registration portal for large frontier AI developers like OpenAI and Anthropic, who must register by January 1, 2027 under the RAISE Act. New York opened a registration portal Tuesday for large frontier AI developers, including Anthropic and OpenAI. They must register by January 1, 2027. The RAISE Act covers companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue. They must publish safety frameworks on their websites, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, and issue public model transparency reports. A new office called DIGIT will implement the law. Penalties can reach $1 million for one violation and $3 million for later ones. Governor Kathy Hochul also launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research at Binghamton University.

item.title: England's university regulator says AI makes coursework grading "close to impossible"
item.description: The Office for Students, England's university regulator, says AI makes grading coursework "close to impossible" and recommends a return to "AI-free assessment" such as written exams. England's university regulator, the Office for Students, says AI has made it "close to impossible" to grade coursework. It recommends that institutions in England return to traditional exams and in-person presentations, which it calls "AI-free assessment". The Guardian reported the story. The Decoder adds that an investigation found students having ChatGPT write entire papers undetected, without being able to recall basic content afterward. The Decoder also reports that universities face sanctions if they do not adopt AI-proof exam formats. The stated aim is to protect the credibility of degrees.

item.title: Report: Apple has a new Mac app coming to ease running local AI models
item.description: 9to5mac reports Apple has a new Mac app coming that is meant to make running local AI models easy. 9to5mac reports that Apple has a new Mac app coming. The app is meant to make running local AI models easy. The story was also shared on Hacker News. The source text gives no other details. It does not say when the app will ship, what it is called, which models it supports, or which Macs it will run on. The same page also carries a separate headline saying iOS 27.2.1 has fixes for security issues in Messages, AirPlay, and more. The source text does not expand on that item either.

item.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed from Moonshot AI now available on Amazon Bedrock
item.description: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed is now on Amazon Bedrock, with Moonshot AI reporting 2–3 times the speed of Kimi K3.1 Pro. Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed from Moonshot AI is now on Amazon Bedrock. It is a post-trained version of Kimi K3 with the same 3T-class open-weight architecture and 1-million-token context window. Moonshot AI says the extra post-training targets long-horizon agentic work and fewer factual errors. Moonshot AI also reports 2–3 times the speed of Kimi K3.1 Pro. It uses the same endpoint, APIs and features as Kimi K3, so existing Kimi K3 users can try it by changing the model ID. It supports tool calling, structured output, configurable reasoning, image input and streaming. The Flex tier costs half the Standard price.

item.title: Apple Researchers Propose Faster Maximum Inner Product Search for RAG
item.description: Apple researchers presented a paper at ICML 2026 detailing how small neural networks can amortize maximum inner product search to speed up RAG retrieval. Maximum inner product search is central to retrieval-augmented generation. Apple researchers presented a paper at ICML 2026 proposing to train small neural networks offline for a fixed database of keys. This approach learns how to route queries toward their best match faster. Traditional methods group keys into clusters and compare queries against centroids, which can cause errors. By treating the mapping function as a support function from convex analysis, the researchers trained SupportNet to learn the support function and KeyNet to directly output the best-matching key vector.

item.title: AWS details agent evaluation options in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
item.description: AWS explains how to evaluate production agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using built-in, DeepEval and AutoEval evaluators, starting from business outcomes rather than metric names. An AWS Machine Learning Blog post lays out how to evaluate agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. It says teams should define success in business terms, break it into observable behaviors, and map each behavior to an evaluator at trace or session level. AgentCore offers three evaluator sources. Built-in evaluators are authored and quality-tested by AWS, referenced by ID such as Builtin.GoalSuccessRate. Third-party managed evaluators come from DeepEval and AutoEval, with AgentCore hosting the code and running inference. Custom evaluators start from a built-in or third-party one, so you can swap in your own model and change the prompt or rubric.

item.title: Nvidia's GR00T 2 learns robot tasks from human videos, with mixed success rates
item.description: Nvidia's GR00T 2 predicts video of a robot arm doing a task, learned from human videos, to cut teleoperation, with 10 to 80 percent success. Nvidia introduced GR00T 2, a model meant to cut the hours engineers spend teleoperating robots. It works as a world-action model, which calculates the next movement and a short video of the immediate future at the same time. Nvidia trained it on more than a thousand GB300 chips, using about 400,000 hours of head-camera video of people doing tasks. In lab tests, a robot with five-fingered hands lit a match, sliced a banana and tossed packages onto a conveyor belt without task-specific teleoperation. Success rates ranged from 10 to 80 percent. The team says the model does not yet process direct touch sensor data and sometimes misses subtle errors like half-turned screws.

item.title: OpenAI workshop shows Codex cloud handoff, voice control and personal agents
item.description: At the AI Engineer Code Summit, OpenAI engineers showed how Codex now blends local and cloud work, uses voice, and pairs with personal agents called dots. OpenAI hosted a workshop called "New Ways of Working with Codex" at the AI Engineer Code Summit. Developer Experience engineers Dominik Kundel and Charlie Guo led it. Codex launched in May 2025 as a cloud-based agent for parallel tasks. Codex Cloud version 2 was announced after DevDay in late September. You publish an environment once and run multiple tasks in isolated instances. Kundel said local and cloud Codex are "merging together" and that he asks Codex to push a branch and start a cloud thread. Guo uses voice as a control plane. He said dots feel a little awkward to work with as a Codex power user.

item.title: Immich listed on site tracking open source projects banning AI-generated contributions
item.description: A site called osssaysno.com lists open source projects that ban AI-generated contributions, and it includes the immich-app/immich photo and video project under policy. A page on osssaysno.com is titled "OSS projects banning AI-generated contributions". It was shared on Hacker News under the same title. One entry in the list is immich-app/immich, described as a high performance self-hosted photo and video management solution. The entry is marked as Policy. The source text does not give the wording of the policy, the date it was set, or the reasons behind it. It also does not say how many other projects are on the list or which ones they are.

item.title: OneLake external-location support for Azure Databricks Unity Catalog reaches GA in Fabric
item.description: Supported Unity Catalog-managed data can now be stored directly in OneLake, generally available in Fabric and in preview on the Azure Databricks side. Microsoft says OneLake external-location support for Azure Databricks Unity Catalog is now generally available in Microsoft Fabric. OneLake Security is enabled by default for Azure Databricks Storage items. On the Azure Databricks side, the feature is in preview. Supported Unity Catalog-managed data can be stored directly in OneLake. Azure Databricks keeps providing compute and Unity Catalog management. OneLake provides the storage destination and Fabric-side data-access controls. Microsoft says this can reduce data copies, synchronization pipelines and separate access management across storage locations. The release builds on an earlier Beta announcement.

item.title: VulnCheck report: Project Glasswing findings outpace fixes after seven months
item.description: VulnCheck says Anthropic's Project Glasswing has 37,966 findings but only 217 marked fixed, and just 2 of 442 tracked CVEs were exploited. VulnCheck's Patrick Garrity reports on Project Glasswing seven months in. He has tracked 442 CVEs attributable to Anthropic, about 0.5% of the 93,450 CVEs published this year. Only 2 were exploited in the wild. Anthropic's ledger lists 37,966 findings, with 7,349 (19.4%) made public and 217 marked fixed. About 1,654 are duplicates and 419 are withdrawn. Since September, nearly 12,000 findings were added and 15 more fixes recorded. Anthropic's claimed true positive rate rose from 90.8% to 94.2%, which VulnCheck questions.

item.title: Microsoft Fabric Blog Details Evolution of CI/CD in Fabric Warehouse
item.description: Microsoft Fabric is evolving CI/CD for Fabric Warehouse to support software engineering practices like Git versioning and automated deployments. Building and operating a data warehouse is increasingly a software engineering discipline. Teams want to develop warehouse changes in isolation, version them in Git, review them through pull requests, promote them safely across environments, and automate the entire process using existing CI/CD systems. Over recent releases, CI/CD in Fabric Warehouse has evolved around this lifecycle. DacFx established a common schema deployment foundation. Pre and post-deployment scripts expanded deployments beyond schema changes. Warehouse Item Definition APIs opened the same lifecycle to automation, creating a more complete CI/CD lifecycle from developing database changes to deploying them.

item.title: Christian Bird Presented AI, Activity, and Outcomes in Software Engineering
item.description: Christian Bird presented a seminar at UC Irvine on October 30, 2026, about AI, activity, and outcomes in software engineering. Christian Bird from Dryden Technology Group gave a 21-minute seminar at UC Irvine on October 30, 2026, titled Why aren't we shipping faster now? AI, activity, and outcomes in software engineering. The talk included slides, handouts, and associated papers covering topics such as the activity-outcome gap, writing code versus shipping code across generations of AI coding tools, code review agents on bug detection, and developer GenAI tool use.

item.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2: up to 30% faster than 5.1, with an optional fast mode
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, models that generate output up to 30% faster than 5.1 and cost $8 per million input tokens. Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, which it says improve coding, reasoning and vision. They are the same underlying model. Fable has cybersecurity and biology safeguards and is open to all users. Mythos is available to organizations through verification programs. Output is up to 30% faster than 5.1, at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. An optional fast mode speeds generation up to 2.5 times, at $16 and $80. On FrontierCode, Fable 5.2 scores 49.1% at Xhigh effort. Both models are on Amazon Bedrock.
